newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks start down on Dow, profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks start down on Dow, profit-taking.

text.p: Mexican stocks opened down in slow, cautious trade on Tuesday as declining Mexican ADRs on Wall Street prompted profit-taking on key blue chips on the bourse, dealers said.

"It is a little nervous; they're taking profits on some blue chips, like Cifra, Ahmsa and Alfa. Trade balance figures were a little disappointing, too," a desk trader said. The leading IPC share index was down 7.28 points in the opening minutes of trade, or 0.18 percent, at 3,977.74.
"Dealing is slow, with some selling in line with the slump on the Dow Jones," a floor trader added.
Retail chain Cifra had receded 10 centavos to 13.20 pesos, after gaining strongly on Monday on what traders said was speculation over a forthcoming deal with Wal-Mart Stores Inc.
Steelmaker Ahmsa was meanwhile off 12 centavos to 18.10 pesos, while conglomerate Alfa had shed 20 centavos to 46.30 pesos.
The Finance Ministry said early on Monday Mexico posted a trade surplus of $109 million in April, compared with $385.74 million predicted by a Reuters survey of Mexico City financial firms MEX22.
Dealers said trade data had little impact on Monday because U.S. markets were closed for Memorial Day.
Trading volume .TV.MX was slow at 1.8 million shares traded.
Market heavyweight Telmex was off two centavos to 17.38 pesos. The telecom firm's ADRS were meanwhile off 1/2 on Wall Street, on the back of the Dow Jones, which had fallen 27.20 points to 7,318.71.
"As it didn't break through at 4,000 points, it seems to be heading towards support at 3,960 to gather strength," a desk trader said.

On the broad market, of 40 stocks traded, just three had gained while 20 were down. Traders said stocks on the gainers' list .PG.MX had moved at very thin volume and did not represent broad market trends.
